headline: NLW's account of Spawn, a 10-person gaming startup whose persistent agent fleet spent $3.1 million on tokens in a month, led the day. Dwarkesh Patel's interview with biographer Robert Caro on how Robert Moses and Lyndon Johnson used power offered a different view of what it takes to build.

themes.title: A startup run by an agent fleet
themes.body: NLW details Jacob Sandbury's playbook for Spawn, which runs a small human team alongside a persistent agent fleet. Spawn spent $3.1 million on tokens last month, 30 times its payroll, and shipped 77,000 code changes, about 108 an hour. Sandbury says only Anthropic's models can do the work and that agent-to-agent communication grows much faster than the work. NLW suspects the approach is hard to retrofit.

themes.title: Robert Caro on power and building
themes.body: Caro tells Dwarkesh Patel that Robert Moses began as an idealist before hardening into ruthlessness, evicting tens of thousands for the Cross Bronx Expressway. Patel cites the Second Avenue subway: about 50 years of building and over $4 billion for a mile and a half. Caro argues that people said government could not build in the 1920s too, and Moses built anyway.

themes.title: Legacy businesses fund AI
themes.body: NLW's headlines include Amazon and Intel earnings that he says show legacy businesses subsidizing AI, legal AI startup Crosby bidding for the assets of bankrupt law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges, Democrats demanding that Trump's Grok logs be preserved, and a New York Times report on Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy.

whyItMatters: When token spend can run at thirty times payroll in an agent-run company, model selection, coordination overhead and AI budgets become architecture decisions, and NLW's view that the model is hard to retrofit argues for piloting it in a new unit.

episodes.title: How the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World Works
episodes.summary: Headlines cover legal AI startup Crosby's bid for bankrupt law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges' assets, Amazon and Intel earnings showing legacy businesses subsidizing AI, Democrats demanding Trump's Grok logs be preserved, Granola dictation, and a NYT report on Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy. The main episode details Jacob Sandbury's playbook for Spawn, a 10-person gaming startup run by a persistent agent fleet.

episodes.title: What Robert Caro learned about power after studying it for 50 years
episodes.summary: Dwarkesh Patel interviews biographer Robert Caro about Robert Moses and Lyndon Johnson, how power is acquired, used and lost, and whether America needs a Moses-type builder today. Caro also discusses his interviewing and writing methods, material cut from his books, his archive, and the loneliness of the Texas Hill Country and of his own work.
